key_idea: Every order forces exactly three hand actions at fixed times t-2d, t-d and t; the busiest second needs ceil(actions/2) cooks.
sketch: Since cook time and serve time are exact, the place, flip and remove moments of each patty are fully determined: t-2d, t-d, t. Count how many actions fall on each second using a map. Cooks are interchangeable and each performs up to two actions per second, so the answer is ceil(max count / 2). O(n log n). Pitfall: forgetting that the placement and the removal also cost a hand, not only the flip.
